title: Portfolio v2
description: The site you're reading. A monospace portfolio set entirely in Courier Prime, rebuilt from scratch around the content instead of the chrome — file-based routing, three languages and light/dark themes.
problem: v1 was a tech demo first and a portfolio second. The code-editor frame was the whole idea, and it worked — but it put a layer of interface between a visitor and the actual work, and it only really landed for people who already knew what a code editor was. I wanted the opposite: something that gets out of the way.
approach: One typeface for everything — Courier Prime — and a layout built from hairline rules, index numbers and a single accent colour, so hierarchy comes from spacing and weight rather than decoration. Routing is file-based: a .vue file dropped into src/pages becomes a route and declares its own nav label and title. All the content lives in three data files, so adding a project or an album is one object, not a new component.
outcome: Six routes, three languages and a third less JavaScript than v1. Language follows the domain — .cat opens in Catalan, .es in Spanish, .com in English — and the theme follows the operating system until you override it. The live parts survived the rewrite: GitHub stats, Spotify now playing, and the Cloudflare R2 gallery.
learnings: Domain-based language detection is three lines of code and removes an entire decision from the visitor. It should be the default, not the fallback.
Keeping translations next to the content instead of in a separate catalogue kept 'add a project' a one-file job — the thing that made v1 pleasant to maintain.
Monospace forces honesty about hierarchy. With one weight axis and no display face to hide behind, anything that isn't earning its place is obvious.
